newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran denies role in attack against Saddam's son.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies role in attack against Saddam's son.

text.p: Iran denied on Monday any involvement in an assassination attempt last month on the son of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein after Bagdhad accused it of sheltering an opposition group which had claimed responsibility for the attack.

"We deny any kind of involvement, be it official or unofficial, direct of indirect of the Iranian government in any attempt against the government of Iraq," Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati told reporters.
He was commenting on Iraqi accusations that Iran was behind the attack in Baghdad on December 12 which wounded Uday Hussein.
Iraq last week asked the United Nations to force Tehran to hand over the alleged perpetrators. Iraq had previously accused Iran of being linked to the crime.
Velayati said it was not the first time that the Iraqi government had made "baseless" accusations against Iran.

"This is the easiest way to justify the chaotic situation there (in Iraq). But throwing accusations at others cannot solve their problems," Velayati said, adding that the attack "goes back to internal problems of the Iraqi government".
